text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 2.7% today as crude oil prices climbed sharply and refining margins expanded. Global oil hit $123.10 per barrel while the U.S. benchmark reached $103.37—a meaningful move upward. This matters for ConocoPhillips because it's an integrated oil and gas company that profits both from higher crude prices and from the spread between crude costs and refined product prices, which surged today after strikes on refineries in Russia and the Middle East disrupted supply and pushed diesel prices higher.

The broader trend accelerating this move is geopolitical: Iranian attacks on tanker traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries are tightening global crude and refined fuel supplies. Competitors Chevron and Exxon hit all-time highs today on the same refining margin surge, signaling that the market is repricing energy stocks upward as it absorbs the reality that regional conflicts are now materially constraining supply.
